long_biography.plain_text:
When Warren Taylor sold his Ford dealership, his son Terry used savings from working there to build an operation of his own. He opened a used-car lot across the road and then bought a new-car franchise in Daytona Beach. Further Ford and Toyota purchases followed as banks and manufacturers gained confidence in him.

Taylor organised each acquisition as a local business, while his West Palm Beach office supplied advertising, property and management services across the group. Dealership real estate, close scrutiny of daily figures and income from financing, maintenance and parts helped the network endure the financial crisis. Its stronger position then allowed him to buy dealerships from owners forced to retreat.
